title: lsline
summary: Add least-squares fit lines to scatter-style plots.

gpu_support.notes: `lsline` inspects existing graphics objects and adds line graphics objects. It does not perform numeric GPU computation or mutate GPU-resident tensors.

description: `lsline` appends least-squares fit lines to eligible scatter-style series in the current or specified axes. It matches MATLAB's compatibility surface for adding fit lines to scatter plots and marker-only line plots, returning the created line handle or handles when requested.
behaviors: `lsline()` scans the current axes and adds one least-squares line for each visible eligible scatter-style plot.
`lsline(ax)` targets the specified axes without changing other axes.
Eligible plots include scatter plots and marker-only line plots. Ordinary line plots with a visible connecting line are ignored.
Non-finite X/Y pairs are skipped when computing the fit. A vertical or constant-X eligible series produces a horizontal least-squares line at the mean Y value.
If no eligible plots are present, RunMat returns an empty `0x0` handle array.
The returned line handle is compatible with `get` and `set` for line properties such as `XData`, `YData`, `Color`, `LineStyle`, `LineWidth`, and `DisplayName`.

examples.description: Add a least-squares line to a scatter plot

faqs.question: How is lsline related to refline?
faqs.answer: `lsline` only computes least-squares fit lines for eligible scatter-style plots. `refline` can do the same when called without coefficients, but it also accepts explicit slope/intercept coefficients for drawing arbitrary reference lines.

faqs.question: Does lsline fit every plot in the axes?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB-style `lsline` is intended for scatter-style data. RunMat fits scatter plots and marker-only line plots and ignores connected line plots, surfaces, bars, and other graphics objects.
